_comment: Import policy for scripts/check-import-graph.py. Encodes plan section 3.2's allowed-dependency matrix. known_cycles are MEASURED on the current tree, not invented: the plan (P0.4) says to record existing cycles rather than fix them during a structural step, and to block only NEW ones.
_known_cycles_note: The first is a genuine 4-module cycle: controlled_emulation imports emulation_plan, which imports investigation, which imports static_analysis, which imports back. The second is the service/tool_execution pair, where tool_execution needs the service surface and the service dispatches tools. Both are pre-existing and are NOT to be fixed inside a structural step; they must be unwound through the ports in P1.2 if at all. Any cycle NOT listed here fails --strict.
_forbidden_edges_note: Direction rules from plan section 3.2: facts/static/emulation/tools/intake must not import the service or the report layer, and facts/ must not depend on emulation/. The flat-module names are listed alongside the future package names because the migration leaves shims that keep both names alive; enforcing only the package names would let a reverse edge survive under the old name. The `service -> forbidden` direction is NOT encoded because service.py legitimately orchestrates every layer: plan section 3.2 places task/ above all of them.
_known_violations_note: MEASURED pre-existing violation of the rule above: persist_how imports reporting, and plan section 3.2's allow-list for the layer that owns persist_how does not include the report layer ('未列出的边默认禁止'). It is RECORDED rather than fixed, because plan P0.4 forbids rewriting business logic during a structural step and P1.4 forbids smuggling a behaviour change into one. --strict therefore fails only on violations NOT in this list, so a NEW reverse edge is still blocked. Unwinding this one belongs with the P1.2 ports.
